channel.title: Submarine Telecoms Forum - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Submarine Telecoms Forum (subtelforum.com)

item.title: Nouadhibou EllaLink Cable Station 46% Complete
item.description: Mauritania’s Nouadhibou EllaLink landing station is 46% complete, with service targeted for Q1 2027 after works finish end-2026.

item.title: Digital Realty Expands to Lisbon for Subsea Data Centre
item.description: Digital Realty enters Portugal by acquiring a Lisbon data centre, boosting proximity to Carcavelos subsea cable landings; ready early 2027.

item.title: Hawaiian Telcom Selects IT for Kunoa North Cable
item.description: Hawaiian Telcom selects IT International Telecom to design and install the Kunoa North inter-island subsea fiber system in Hawaii by 2028.

item.title: The Carrier Guide to 2026: Traffic, Tech and Trends
item.description: Mattias Fridström explores carrier trends for 2026 in this article from SubTel Forum Issue 146, covering AI, traffic growth and security.

item.title: Integrated Digital Connectivity Drives Africa’s Growth
item.description: Chris Wood explores Africa’s digital growth in this article from SubTel Forum Issue 146, covering cables, data centers and cloud.

item.title: Technology-Driven Cable Market Cycles
item.description: José Chesnoy examines technology-driven cycles in the submarine cable industry in this article from SubTel Forum Issue 146.

item.title: What Is It With This Direct United States Telegraph Cable?
item.description: Derek Cassidy explores the Direct United States Telegraph Cable in this article from SubTel Forum Issue 146.

item.title: SubTel Forum Magazine #147 – Finance & Legal – OUT NOW!
item.description: Issue 147 of SubTel Forum explores industry limits, FCC cable licensing reforms, Arctic broadband, AI cable strategy, and subsea risk.

item.title: Marshall Islands Advances Pacific Connect Cable Project
item.description: Marshall Islands joins Pacific Connect to deploy Iokwe subsea cable, boosting resilience, speed, and global digital access.

item.title: Amazon Says Drone Activity Disrupts AWS Bahrain Region
item.description: Drone activity disrupts AWS Bahrain region, forcing workload shifts and exposing risks to cloud infrastructure in conflict zones.
